title: CI/CD for Private VPC Terraform: linting, plan/apply pipelines & policy-as-code
creator: Liam Chen
description: Implement end-to-end CI/CD for the Private (VPC) Terraform modules used by Redwood Private deployments. Deliverables: standardized linting and static checks, gated plan/apply pipelines in GitHub Actions (or buildkite), policy-as-code enforcement using OPA/Conftest rules, canary upgrade path for module upgrades, and automated post-apply health checks. This work reduces risk for on-prem/VPC upgrades, speeds safe rollouts, and ensures infra changes meet security/compliance policies before reaching production tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Repository-level GitHub Actions workflow (or Buildkite) runs tflint, terraform fmt check, and tfsec/Checkov on every PR
Plan stage runs terraform plan with -out and uploads plan artifact; Conftest/OPA policies evaluate plan and block merges on policy violations
Apply stage is gated: only runs from release branch or after an approved manual review; supports a canary apply to a staging VPC then a controlled rollout to production VPCs
Automated post-apply health checks execute (VPC peering, route table, KMS key access, endpoint reachability, example service deploy) and surface failures to on-call and PR
Policy rules codified in repo under infra/policies/ and testable locally using conftest; documented policy exceptions process
Pipelines produce traceable artifacts: plan JSON, policy evaluation report, and health check runbook link
Security review completed and signed off by Security team before enabling auto-apply in production
Documentation and runbook added to Confluence; example workflows and local dev guide included in repo README
tasks: Design CI flow for module repositories (lint -> plan -> policy -> apply -> health-check)
Add tflint + custom rules to infra shared toolset
Integrate tfsec and Checkov scans for common misconfigurations
Implement Conftest/OPA policies that operate on terraform plan JSON (network, iam, kms, logging, encryption)
Create GitHub Actions workflows: terraform-plan.yml and terraform-apply.yml with required secrets and approvals
Implement canary apply job: target staging VPC tag set and test tenant list
Create health-check suite (python/bash) that validates networking and key access post-apply
Add policy exception and escalation flow in docs (who approves, SLA for review)
Add e2e test: module upgrade path + rollback on health-check failure
Coordinate security review and get signoff (Security ticket linked)
Ship docs and example PR template for infra changes
plan_pipeline: github-actions:terraform-plan.yml (runs on PR, saves plan.json artifact)
apply_pipeline: github-actions:terraform-apply.yml (manual approval step; requires security sign-off for prod)
policy_checks: Conftest (rego) policies under infra/policies/rego: network_allowlist.rego, kms_encryption.rego, iam_no_wildcard.rego
OPA evaluation executed during plan stage; failure blocks merge
tfsec + Checkov provide supplemental findings and are surfaced in PR comments
health_checks: vpc_connectivity_test.sh: verifies route tables, subnets, and peering
kms_access_check.py: ensures RBAC and envelope access for tenant buckets
service_probe.sh: deploys a small test pod/service to private cluster (when applicable) and hits endpoint
dns_resolution_test: validates private hosted zone entries
rollout_strategy: Canary-first: run apply against staging-tagged VPCs (one tenant), run health checks for 30m; if green, progressive apply to batch of production VPCs with 15m health-check windows and automatic rollback on failures
notes: We should reuse the shared infra-actions library for secrets, tfenv, and state locking (S3/Dynamo) to avoid duplication
Consider Terragrunt wrapper compatibility — ensure plan pipeline supports both native terraform and terragrunt invocations
Security team prefers OPA rules but requested a Conftest wrapper for local dev friendliness
We need an allowlist of high-risk modules that always require manual review (eg. route table changes, IAM role assumptions)
